question:
Select the word segment that can substitute the bracketed words correctly and complete the sentence meaningfully.

(My husband and I) are from Varanasi.
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Both of us.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence specifies that both the speaker and their husband are from Varanasi.
 
• The phrase **“Both of us”** is appropriate because it clearly refers to two people together, i.e., the speaker and their husband.
 
• Other options like **“Either of us”** imply only one of them is from Varanasi, which is incorrect.
 
• **“Everyone of us”** and **“Each one of us”** are incorrect because they are generally used for groups larger than two.

Correct sentence: *Both of us are from Varanasi.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of “Both of us”:**

 
 
• **Meaning:** Refers to two people collectively.
 
• **Example:** Both of us love traveling.
 
 
 
• **Usage of “Either of us”:**

 
 
• **Meaning:** Refers to one of two people.
 
• **Example:** Either of us can pick you up from the station.
 
 
 
• **Usage of “Everyone of us”:**

 
 
• **Meaning:** Refers to all individuals in a group.
 
• **Example:** Everyone of us enjoyed the picnic.
 
 
 
• **Usage of “Each one of us”:**

 
 
• **Meaning:** Refers to every individual in a group individually.
 
• **Example:** Each one of us contributed to the project.
